title: Master the Art of Storytelling
coreMove: Turn evidence into human movement so the audience can feel why the idea matters.
sourcePressure: The source uses Bryan Stevenson's TED talk on injustice, Aristotle's ethos/logos/pathos triad, Rosa Parks, and Kurt Vonnegut to show story as the exchange vessel for ideas. Pathos carries much of the talk while logos and ethos support it.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version says stories beat facts. The useful version says story lets facts reach the audience through a person, a tension, and a consequence.

sourceAnchors.name: Bryan Stevenson
sourceAnchors.detail: the source uses Stevenson's talk on injustice as the primary anchor for mixing prison-system data with stories from life and family
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Bryan Stevenson lets the numbers carry a human face before asking the room to carry the argument.

sourceAnchors.name: Aristotle
sourceAnchors.detail: the source explains the talk through Aristotle's rhetoric triad of ethos, logos, and pathos
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Aristotle's old triad still names the balance: credibility, reason, and feeling have to work in the same direction.

sourceAnchors.name: Rosa Parks
sourceAnchors.detail: the source lists Rosa Parks as a usable proper noun in the chapter's storytelling support
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A name like Rosa Parks reminds the room that public ideas often survive because they have a person inside them.

hook: data slide fails until story saves it
tryThisNow: add a hero to your talk
write down a beginning, middle, and end

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.audience: a law professor asking alumni to fund case investigation hours
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether donors hear billable hours or the years one wrong file can steal
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she moves the exoneration statistics after the first client letter and lets the letter create the human path into the data
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a creased prison envelope beside a stack of case-hour invoices

exampleSpecs.audience: an infection-control nurse briefing surgeons on handoff compliance
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a sterile checklist feels like bureaucracy or like the moment that protected one patient
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he starts with the recovery-room call that almost went wrong, then shows how the compliance chart explains the risk at scale
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a red phone light blinking over a recovery-room desk

exampleSpecs.audience: a conservation organizer speaking to skeptical landowners
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether acreage maps become a story of one herd finding a safe path
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she asks where the tagged elk will cross, lets the room guess wrong, then reveals the map and tells the calf story that makes the corridor matter
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a satellite collar dot frozen near a highway overpass

exampleSpecs.audience: a trainer welcoming first-year electrical apprentices
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether safety rules feel like scolding or like inherited craft protection
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after an apprentice jokes about lockout tags, he tells the story of the retired foreman who kept one burned tag in his toolbox, then teaches the rule
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a faded red lockout tag clipped to a dented toolbox latch

exampleSpecs.audience: an actuary explaining flood-model changes to claims managers
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a model revision sounds like math housekeeping or a family waiting longer for repair money
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: you watch her replace the opening formula with a claim timeline for one flooded basement, then use the model to show why the delay repeats
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a damp claim folder curling at the corner under a desk lamp

exampleSpecs.audience: a principal presenting reading-intervention results to a board
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the board sees a percentile table or a student who can finally read the bus sign home
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he introduces one student's bus-sign moment before showing the full intervention table, so the evidence has a person attached
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a laminated bus route card held at the edge of a boardroom lectern

skillTargets: identify when story supports evidence rather than replacing it
choose a human path into data
analyze ethos, logos, and pathos in a presentation choice
evaluate whether a story has tension and consequence

tryThisNowSpec: Take one number from an upcoming talk and write the person, tension, and consequence that the number should help the audience understand.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
